body.title: Design one pilot activity, with no place required
body.body:
## What is delivered
A design for one pilot activity — local or remote, no place required: who coordinates it, what support it offers, how participation is measured, and the condition under which it ends.

Small enough that one person could run it, specific enough that someone could say it failed.

## Why it is needed
This component starts with an activity, not with a building. A physical centre is only considered after there is evidence of demand and of something that can sustain itself, and right now there is no instrument that would produce that evidence.

There is no inventory of properties, no staff, no budget, no licences and no confirmed pilot. This function is what turns a long-term idea into something testable this month.

## Where to start
The ending condition is the part people skip. A pilot that cannot fail teaches nothing, so decide up front what result would mean "do not do this again".

## Prior material

Drayker has earlier work on this subject in its own knowledge base — drafts, mostly in Portuguese, written before the public repositories took their current shape. It is not published yet. If you take this function, say so in the thread and the relevant material will be published alongside it, so you are consolidating and arguing with existing thinking rather than starting from a blank page.

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest. Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/fn/

body.title: Posts, stations and embassies distinguished
body.body:
Alignment pass across the `draykerdk` organization, on the branch `alinhamento/2026-09` in every affected repository.

## Changes

- docs: posts, stations and embassies as published in ch. 52 of the book (2.7.1)
- docs: remove book citations

## Across the organization

- Governance corrected: PAP is Projects & Applications, DFMP is the DFM proposal process, the founding account is `Hyadhuad`, and the governance horizon runs from the founding Embassy through the DAF into PAP.
- The veto chain specified in UID: signed, hash-linked vetoes that carry their real grounds even when anonymous; vetoes weighed by grounds, not counted; one veto with grounds beyond the decision's scope can lead to an adjustment after advanced triage.
- Direction states 2033 as the objective, measured by what works rather than by the date.
- Intelligence is a partner, never the master.
- English is the canonical documentation language.
- Documentation states its own claims and does not cite outside books as authority.

Documentation only. Nothing here claims an implemented system.

Supersedes #4, closed when the branch was renamed.

body.title: Embassies as autonomous zones, pure autonomous zones at sea and countries as members
body.body_html:
Aligns this repository with the decisions of October 2026:

  • member councils formed for each question instead of an independent judicial panel chosen by lot;
  • no forks or open-code claims for Dk: auditable through Dknowledge and DFM by permission level, with divergence tested in parallel;
  • Dk Global decides only inside the space the constitution gives it, open to representation, proposals and justified vetoes;
  • units of account instead of a token economy.

body.title: stations: make the sovereignty non-scope precise
body.body:
## What changes
In component.yml, "Any unilateral claim of state territorial sovereignty" becomes "Any claim over a state's territory without that state's consent. Pure autonomous zones on the high seas need no cession."

## Why
The README describes pure autonomous zones on the high seas, where no state needs to cede territory. The old non-scope line could be read as excluding them.

body.title: stations: stations are Drayker properties; autonomous zones include housing
body.body:
## What changes
- **README:** a station does not need to be an autonomous zone; it is a Drayker property anywhere in the world, much like an office for a given purpose, from study and research to work. Autonomous zones, at sea or on ceded territory, include housing for the people who live and work there. The non-scope line now reads "A property, residency or relocation offer available today".
- **component.yml:** "A commercial property, speculative real estate or residency offer" becomes "Speculative real estate, or property and residency sold as products"; the scope names stations as properties and housing in autonomous zones.

## Why
Founder's clarification (2026-10-05). The previous non-scope excluded properties and residency as such, which contradicts the design.

body.title: Embassies are named for becoming sovereign territories
body.body:
## What changed
- **README:** "The name does not by itself create a diplomatic status: conditions, guarantees and responsibilities depend on the concrete agreements." becomes "That is where the name comes from: an embassy becomes a sovereign territory of Drayker bordering other countries, and its conditions, guarantees and responsibilities are set in the concrete bilateral agreements."

## Why
Embassies are born from bilateral agreements with countries and become sovereign territories of Drayker bordering other countries, usually autonomous zones on ceded land; that is the reason for the name. The rest of the paragraph (stations and posts as Drayker properties anywhere, pure autonomous zones at sea, the Embassy of Drayker as the founding core) already matches and is unchanged.
